population_note: The de facto authorities' estimate of the people present on 1 January 2026: their census of February 2011, carried forward with each year's births and arrivals added and deaths and departures taken away (their statistics committee's yearbook, table 1.11). sex_ratio_note: The de facto authorities' estimate for 1 January 2026: 115,252 men and 128,725 women. Their census of February 2011 counted 111,885 men and 128,820 women, 86.9 men per 100 women.
ethnicity_note: Nationality as the de facto authorities' census of February 2011 counted it (their statistics committee's yearbook, table 1.12), Georgians and Mingrelians apart as the census lists them. Their tables for later years, to 1 January 2026, keep each district's 2011 shares to within a fifth of a percentage point, so they are not a newer count.

population_note: The de facto authorities' estimates of the people present on 1 January 2026 in the city of Sukhum (65,180) and in the Sukhum district around it (11,212), which they count apart, added together; each is their census of February 2011, carried forward with each year's births and arrivals added and deaths and departures taken away (their statistics committee's yearbook, table 1.11). The map draws no outline for the city, whose centre lies in this one. The line drawn with Gulripshi runs through the city's south-east: by WorldPop's 2020 population grid, about 7% of these people live on the Gulripshi side of it. Georgia's own 2014 census and Geostat's estimates do not cover Abkhazia, and the authorities that count it are recognised by few states.
sex_ratio_note: The de facto authorities' estimate for 1 January 2026: 35,608 men and 40,784 women. Their census of February 2011 counted 33,388 men and 41,057 women, 81.3 men per 100 women.
ethnicity_note: Nationality as the de facto authorities' census of February 2011 counted it (their statistics committee's yearbook, table 1.12), Georgians and Mingrelians apart as the census lists them. Their tables for later years, to 1 January 2026, keep each district's 2011 shares to within a fifth of a percentage point, so they are not a newer count. The city's and the district's counts are added together.

name: Gali

population.note: The de facto authorities redrew the districts here after the war: in 1995 they formed Tkvarcheli district from parts of the Ochamchira and Gal districts, and they count more of Gal's former villages in Ochamchira district. The outlines drawn as Ochamchire and Gali follow the districts as they were before only roughly, and neither holds a district the authorities count: villages of the Ochamchira and Tkvarcheli districts lie in this one, and so does the centre of the town of Ochamchira (5,154 people on 1 January 2026), which the line between this outline and Ochamchire's runs through, while Gal's villages along the Enguri (Chuburkhinji, Otobaia, Tagiloni, Pichori and others; at least 12,066 of the district's 30,356 people at the 2011 census) lie outside it, in the outline drawn as Zugdidi. Ochamchira, Tkvarcheli and Gal districts together had 72,882 people on 1 January 2026 (26,073, 16,458 and 30,351); no figure is written for either outline.

median_age.note: Not published by district: the de facto authorities' statistics committee gives ages from their 2011 census for Abkhazia as a whole only.

sex_ratio.note: Not written: the outline drawn here holds parts of several of the districts the de facto authorities count by, and none of them whole.
